This confirms the mechanism: `PacketHandler`'s constructor always sets `isLoadingLevel = true`, and `packetHandler` is instantiated as a field default (`Minecraft.java:234`) even in singleplayer where there's no network traffic to ever flip it to `false`. So in singleplayer, `packetHandler.isLoadingLevel` stays `true` forever, and before the fix, `if (!packetHandler.isLoadingLevel) { pause(); }` would never pause on ESC — it would just call `Mouse.setGrabbed(false)` instead. The fix adds `|| !isOnline()` to correctly allow pausing in singleplayer regardless of that stale flag.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 3f3305e469b9f5b4a21215fec35b8ef8ea0e6add

## Reasoning
(1) I used `git log -S "isLoadingLevel"` on `Minecraft.java` to find all commits that touched the condition logic around `isLoadingLevel`, then inspected each candidate diff (`abf3813`, `05c8554`, `3f3305e`). I then read the surrounding code (`isOnline()`, `PacketHandler` field initialization/constructor) to understand runtime behavior in singleplayer vs. online mode.

(2) Commit `3f3305e` is the one that introduced the exact `if (!packetHandler.isLoadingLevel){ pause(); } else { Mouse.setGrabbed(false); }` block that the bug-fix commit (`be39b28`) later patches by adding `|| !isOnline()` to the condition. Before `3f3305e`, pressing ESC unconditionally called `pause()`. That commit made pausing conditional solely on `packetHandler.isLoadingLevel`, without accounting for singleplayer games.

(3) Supporting evidence: `PacketHandler`'s constructor (`src/main/java/com/mojang/minecraft/net/PacketHandler.java:50-55`) unconditionally sets `isLoadingLevel = true`, and `Minecraft.packetHandler` is instantiated as a field default (`new PacketHandler(this)` at `Minecraft.java:234`) regardless of whether the game is online or singleplayer. Since `isLoadingLevel` is only toggled by network packet handling (`setLoadingLevel(false)` calls live inside packet-processing code), it never flips to `false` in singleplayer, where no packets are ever processed. Thus after `3f3305e`'s change, pressing ESC in singleplayer would always take the "still loading" branch and never call `pause()` — exactly the bug that `be39b28` fixes by special-casing `!isOnline()`.

I'm highly confident in this attribution since the line modified by the fix is textually identical to the line introduced by `3f3305e`, and the surrounding code fully explains the causal mechanism of the bug.
